questions: How many devices did you fabricate and measure, and how many showed the e/3 resonances, the even-odd effect and the 2e/3 regime? Methods describe one device over two cooldowns (p. 9), and the author contributions say "M.V. fabricated the devices" (p. 8).
Why were the other devices set aside?
Which ranges of VT, Vdot, bias and field did you measure beyond the windows in Table I, and over how much of that space does the 2e/3 periodicity of Fig. 4f appear?
What does the second-best dataset of the 2e/3 regime look like? Table I suggests all of Fig. 4 comes from the second (DC) cooldown; did the first cooldown show the even-odd effect or the merging?

Did you check gate leakage in the fractional regime, and in Fig. 4f and Extended Data Fig. 10 do all resonance lines share one slope, as a single dot would give, or is there a second family that could come from a nearby trap?

Could the missing sector in Fig. 4g be a transition that still happens but is blockaded in transport, as the quasielectron transitions are at ν = 1, or a sector narrower than your resolution? A temperature or field series at VT = 0.04 V, or a charge sensor, would tell.

Do the diamond heights and slopes at ν = 1/3 give the same lever arm α and capacitance Cd as at ν = 1? Fig. 1 quotes e∆VDC ≈ 2 meV at ν = 1 and EC = (e/3)∆VDC ≈ 300 µeV at ν = 1/3, and an independent α at each filling would test the fixed-geometry assumption behind the e/3 reading of δ.

Was the Fig. 4e alternation reproducible on repeated sweeps at the same settings, and how was the dip-finding algorithm set up for the δ traces, given that Extended Data Fig. 10 notes it "may miss resonances as they emerge"?
